_comment: AUTHORED desired-truth registry of the machine-checkable hard laws (SKY-011). This is the constraint layer of ADR 0003's ambiguity ladder: authored data a DETERMINISTIC gate reads (scripts/check-invariants.sh, Phase 3) — NOT generated, and distinct from inventory/ (observed truth) and docs/generated/ (machine-owned). Rigor comes from the gate consuming this file, not from the JSON itself: an LLM reads it with the same latitude as prose. Each entry carries a one-line 'why' so the load-bearing rationale rides WITH the constraint. Editing ops_managed_pools moves the blast-radius dial and is a docs/system-design.md PR (§2b). Doctrine: docs/decisions/0003-ambiguity-layering-and-format-follows-enforcement.md.

excluded_guests.why: These guests are T3 — the firewall, the front doors, the storage box. The agent must never destroy, stop, re-disk, re-NIC, or pool them. Pool membership is the enforced line: joining any to an ops-managed pool hands the agent full T2 write (VM.Allocate/PowerMgmt/Config.*), so the gate fails any PR where one of these VMIDs appears as a pool member. The svc-tofu provisioning token keeps VM.Allocate/VM.PowerMgmt pool-scoped (never over these); its config-only /vms role (VM.Config.Options/Cloudinit/CDROM) is bound on both nodes, so tofu can config-touch all four (name/tags/onboot/cloud-init/CDROM) but never destroy, stop, re-disk, or re-NIC them. See docs/design/access-and-trust.md (svc-tofu).

guests.name: vm-opnsense
guests.why: the firewall/router itself; DHCP + all inter-VLAN routing depend on it. Never poolable.

guests.name: lxc-caddy-management
guests.why: the Management Caddy (the privileged front door). T3 by constitution §3.

guests.name: lxc-authentik
guests.why: Authentik server administration is T3 (app/provider provisioning is a separate scoped T2 token, not pool membership).

guests.name: vm-unraid
guests.why: Unraid storage host; root over it is T3. Never poolable.

entity_conventions.why: SKY-018 L0: the VMID<->IP law (ADR 0001 / docs/conventions/naming.md) and its DECLARED exceptions. LAW: a guest's VMID = VLAN + 2-digit last octet — VMID/100 matches a declared VLAN either canonically (10015 = VLAN 100) or with the trailing zero dropped (240 = VLAN 20), and the octet is the last two digits — so a guest's address derives from its VMID and self-validates. GATE (check-invariants.sh, 4th law): every RUNNING entity is either mapped (a guest's derived IP is a firewall/DNS host fact; a service has a compose/<project>/ dir) OR a declared exception. Exceptions are drawn from TWO places, so there is one source of truth per kind: the T3 excluded_guests below (never-poolable infra — opnsense/caddy-mgmt/authentik/unraid), and the `exceptions` list here (running guests intentionally off the entity map: off-convention VMIDs or standby/not-serving hosts). Empty today — the lab is clean. Changing declared_vlans is a docs/conventions/naming.md change.

ops_managed_pools.why: THE blast-radius dial. Write blast radius = this pool set (+ ROLE_OPS_SSH_TARGETS + Technitium zones). The gate asserts the ops-managed pools observed in inventory match this declared set — drift either way is a violation (an undeclared pool is as dangerous as a missing one). Changing this set is a docs/system-design.md PR (constitution §2b); it is NOT collected/generated.

pools.why: the ops-managed pool on the core node; current position of the dial.
the ops-managed pool on the network node; current position of the dial.

t3_targets.why: The never-standing-credential list (constitution §2a / §3, AGENTS.md §6). No standing route or credential that can CHANGE any of these — reached only via a dormant alias + per-session credentials, revoked same day. One scoped READ carve-out: OPNsense read is T1 (ADR 0006); the write/admin plane of every entry here stays never-standing. Documented here now as desired truth; future checks (e.g. asserting no standing WRITE token references these) build on it.

targets.name: OPNsense config/admin
targets.why: the firewall/router admin plane — rules, aliases, DHCP, settings, root shell: T3, never a standing WRITE credential. OPNsense READ is T1 (a scoped read-only API credential; the collector strips secrets). See ADR 0006 / docs/design/access-and-trust.md.

targets.name: Authentik server admin
targets.why: flows, policies, users, system settings, outpost tokens, signing keys stay T3 (VMID 837).

targets.name: Proxmox node root
targets.why: root on either hypervisor node is T3.

targets.name: Unraid root
targets.why: root on the storage host (VMID 2020) is T3.

targets.name: Technitium server settings
targets.why: Settings/Administration/DHCP are T3; only Zones view/modify is T2.

secret_patterns.why: Plaintext-secret signatures the gate greps for in tracked, non-encrypted files. Hard law: secrets are sops-encrypted in git (compose/*/.env.sops) or 0600 under /opt/skynet-ops/secrets/ — never plaintext in commits, logs, transcripts, or chat (constitution §2a). A hit fails the PR.

allow.why: sops-encrypted payloads are ciphertext by definition — the intended home for secrets in git.
holds only the age PUBLIC recipient key (age1...), which is not secret.
this file lists the patterns themselves as data; it contains no live secret.

patterns.why: an age PRIVATE key (prefix + bech32 body); the master secret of the whole vault. Must only ever exist at /opt/skynet-ops/secrets/age.key + the survival kit. Requiring the key body means prose that merely mentions the prefix does not trip.
any PEM private key block (OpenSSH/RSA/EC/PKCS8) — SSH or TLS private material must never be committed in plaintext.
a Proxmox API token secret (user@realm!tokenid=UUID) — a live write/read credential to the cluster.
